title: Codebase Vector Search
description:
Separate code base embedding using nomic embed
Script to generate an on-disc sequel light database 
Used to regenerate only when necessary 
Vector search uses simple cosine similarity to start 
Used to augment existing KB memory and Page searches, by adding mCP tooling and chat tool support for searching against the specified code base for symbols and methods. 
Used during agent research to build out the kb, and while using the KB as guidance for what to search for and how to interpret it in context
Embedding step uses a gitignore as default, with optional filters that augment or override the .gitignore for further refinement and focusing of embedded code sources
It would be nice to expose this in the web, with snippets of the source shown for results and links to open the files
Should be able to target multiple directories. Use the memorysmith projects as the targets so we can search our own codebase

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Completed by adding `MemorySmith.App/Services/CodeSearchService.cs`, which builds a reusable SQLite-backed chunk index at `Data/Graph/code-search/code-search.db` for the configured MemorySmith project targets, honors repo `.gitignore` plus include/exclude overrides, and reuses unchanged file chunks instead of re-embedding them. Chat and MCP now expose `memorysmith_code_search` through `MemorySmith.App/Services/ChatToolCatalog.cs`, `MemorySmith.App/Services/ChatServices.cs`, and `MemorySmith.App/Controllers/McpController.cs`, with deterministic code-search intent interception and prompt contract updates. Focused validation passed with `dotnet test .\MemorySmith.Tests\MemorySmith.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~ChatToolCatalogAndInterceptTests|Name~McpToolsList_ExposesWikiSearchTools|Name~McpCodeSearchTool_ReturnsIndexedRepoMatches" --logger "console;verbosity=minimal"`, which reported 25/25 passed.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Follow-up hardening completed for the code-search embedding/import path. `MemorySmith.App/Services/CodeSearchService.cs` now reports live build progress and last-build summary through `CodeSearchStatus.Build`, batches SQLite document rewrites, isolates per-file indexing failures instead of aborting the whole build, reuses unchanged documents on warm builds via persisted metadata plus hashes, and caches repeated exact queries in-process. Chat/MCP now also expose `memorysmith_code_search_status`, while `memorysmith_code_search` accepts `forceRebuild` for an explicit cold rebuild. Focused validation passed with `dotnet test .\MemorySmith.Tests\MemorySmith.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~ChatToolCatalogAndInterceptTests|Name~McpToolsList_ExposesWikiSearchTools|Name~McpCodeSearchTool_ReturnsIndexedRepoMatches|Name~McpCodeSearchStatusTool_ReturnsBuildSummary" --logger "console;verbosity=minimal"` (29/29), and `Scripts\Validate-Repo.ps1` finished green with 392/392 tests plus task, memory, and page validators.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Improved relevance for low-overlap semantic queries by adding synonym-aware query expansion and hybrid vector/lexical reranking with a no-lexical-evidence penalty in `CodeSearchService`. Added regression `SearchAsync_HybridRerankPromotesToolingResultForScrewdriverQuery` to prove `screwdriver` promotes tooling results instead of unrelated high-cosine chunks. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests"` (21/21 passed) and benchmark smoke `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` shows `CodeSearch Screwdriver Query` top hit `MemorySmith.App/Services/ToolCatalog.cs`.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Added a second quality hardening pass: per-document result diversity (`MaxResultsPerDocument`, default `2`) to prevent one file from flooding top-k, plus regression `SearchAsync_DiversifiesResultsAcrossDocuments_WhenSingleFileWouldOtherwiseDominate`. Benchmark smoke now prints warm-query averages for code-search probes. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests"` (22/22 passed). Spotcheck/benchmark: `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` -> screwdriver top hit still `ToolCatalog.cs`; warm averages about `0.56-0.58 ms` over 20 iterations.

comments.author: AgentSmith

Benchmark smoke now emits a compact code-search scorecard pass rate with expected-vs-actual top hits for fast operator spotchecks. comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Normalized memory/tag quality for the wiki corpus by adding audited tag aliases and `tasks` allowlist support in `Data/Policies/tag-policy.json`, then added `project-wiki-code-search-relevance-suite` so recent code-search ranking and benchmark contracts are captured as durable project memory. comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Continued high-ROI search tuning by reducing lexical keyword-stuffing bias in `MemorySmith.App/Services/CodeSearchService.cs` (token-coverage-first lexical scoring with damped frequency bonus), then expanded gates for both quality and performance. Added `SearchAsync_LexicalFallbackDemotesKeywordStuffingAgainstTargetedMatch` in `MemorySmith.Tests/CodeSearchServiceTests.cs`, expanded shared fixture `Data/Benchmarks/code-search-scorecard.json` with `tool utility harness` (5 probes total), and added benchmark-category p95 guard `WarmLatencyDistribution_100QueriesP95Under10Ms` in `MemorySmith.Tests/CodeSearchBenchmarkTests.cs`. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchBenchmarkTests"` (31/31 passed) and `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` (`CodeSearch Relevance Scorecard: 5/5 passed`, warm averages about `0.56-0.58 ms`).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Added token-coverage weighting to hybrid and lexical ranking in `MemorySmith.App/Services/CodeSearchService.cs` so partial token matches are penalized and full-intent matches are boosted, with coverage details surfaced in match reasons. Added regression `SearchAsync_HybridRerankPrefersBroaderTokenCoverageUnderVectorBias` in `MemorySmith.Tests/CodeSearchServiceTests.cs` and tuned coverage weights (`0.65` to `1.15`) after the first conservative range failed this new quality guard. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchBenchmarkTests"` (32/32 passed) and `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` (`CodeSearch Relevance Scorecard: 5/5 passed`, warm averages about `0.54-0.55 ms`).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Implemented full code-search ranking tunability for operator deepdive tuning. Added configurable ranking knobs in `MemorySmith.App/Services/MemorySmithOptions.cs` and defaults in `MemorySmith.App/appsettings.json` (`HybridVectorWeight`, `HybridLexicalWeight`, `ZeroLexicalEvidencePenalty`, `LexicalScoreSaturation`, `LexicalFrequencyBonusScale`, `MaxLexicalFrequencyBonusPerToken`, `MinTokenCoverageWeight`, `MaxTokenCoverageWeight`). `MemorySmith.App/Services/CodeSearchService.cs` now consumes clamped option values instead of hardcoded constants. `MemorySmith.App/Services/AdminSettingsService.cs` now supports decimal setting values and exposes these code-search tuning controls in Admin Search settings. Added regression `SearchAsync_TunableCoverageWeightsCanNeutralizeCoverageBias` in `MemorySmith.Tests/CodeSearchServiceTests.cs` plus governance check `AdminSettings_ExposeCodeSearchRankingTuningKnobs` in `MemorySmith.Tests/TagGovernanceTests.cs`. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchBenchmarkTests|FullyQualifiedName~TagGovernanceTests.AdminSettings_ExposeCodeSearchRankingTuningKnobs"` (34/34 passed) and `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` (`CodeSearch Relevance Scorecard: 5/5 passed`, warm averages about `0.53-0.54 ms`).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Deepdive reliability fix: added cross-setting validation guardrails for tunable code-search ranking settings in `MemorySmith.App/Services/AdminSettingsService.cs`. Admin/API writes now reject invalid combinations where both hybrid weights are zero or where `MinTokenCoverageWeight` exceeds `MaxTokenCoverageWeight`. Validation was updated to evaluate merged pending override JSON state (not stale options snapshots), so sequential admin updates in one session are correctly enforced. Expanded API contract test `AdminSettings_UpdateRequiresAdminAndPersistsAllowedSetting` in `MemorySmith.Tests/AppApiContractTests.cs` to assert rejection/error messaging and non-persistence of invalid combinations. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AppApiContractTests.AdminSettings_UpdateRequiresAdminAndPersistsAllowedSetting|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchBenchmarkTests|FullyQualifiedName~TagGovernanceTests.AdminSettings_ExposeCodeSearchRankingTuningKnobs"` (35/35 passed) and `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` (`CodeSearch Relevance Scorecard: 5/5 passed`, warm averages about `0.53-0.54 ms`).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Deepdive quality/performance fix for sparse lexical prefilter edge cases. Added tunable `VectorPrefilterFullScanFallbackCandidateCount` in `MemorySmith.App/Services/MemorySmithOptions.cs`, defaulted it in `MemorySmith.App/appsettings.json` (`24`), and exposed it in Admin Search settings via `MemorySmith.App/Services/AdminSettingsService.cs`. Updated `MemorySmith.App/Services/CodeSearchService.cs` to run full-index vector fallback when prefilter candidate count is at/below threshold and prefilter results are present (`vector-sparse-fallback` mode), improving semantic recall for sparse lexical queries. Added regressions `SearchAsync_SparsePrefilterFallbackRecoversSemanticTopDocument` and `SearchAsync_SparsePrefilterFallbackCanBeDisabled` in `MemorySmith.Tests/CodeSearchServiceTests.cs`, plus governance coverage update in `MemorySmith.Tests/TagGovernanceTests.cs`. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchBenchmarkTests|FullyQualifiedName~TagGovernanceTests.AdminSettings_ExposeCodeSearchRankingTuningKnobs|FullyQualifiedName~AppApiContractTests.AdminSettings_UpdateRequiresAdminAndPersistsAllowedSetting"` (37/37 passed) and `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` (`CodeSearch Relevance Scorecard: 5/5 passed`, warm averages about `0.53 ms`).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Continued deepdive quality/performance work by adding explicit prefilter-threshold A/B benchmark-category coverage in `MemorySmith.Tests/CodeSearchBenchmarkTests.cs` (`SparsePrefilterThreshold_AB_ImprovesRecallWithBoundedLatencyCost`). The fixture proves threshold impact directly: with fallback disabled, lexical prefilter anchors top hit at `MemorySmith.App/Services/LexicalAnchor.cs`; with fallback enabled, semantic full-scan rescue recovers `MemorySmith.Core/Services/HiddenTrueTop.cs`, while keeping warm latency within a bounded envelope (sample: disabledAvg `0.522 ms`, enabledAvg `0.497 ms`). During validation, a scorecard flake surfaced from process-randomized `string.GetHashCode()` slotting in benchmark test embeddings; fixed by switching `HashEmbeddingProvider` to deterministic FNV-1a token hashing (`ComputeStableHash`) so rank assertions are stable across runs. Validation: `dotnet test MemorySmith.Tests/MemorySmith.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchBenchmarkTests|FullyQualifiedName~CodeSearchServiceTests|FullyQualifiedName~AppApiContractTests.AdminSettings_UpdateRequiresAdminAndPersistsAllowedSetting|FullyQualifiedName~TagGovernanceTests.AdminSettings_ExposeCodeSearchRankingTuningKnobs"` (38/38 passed) and `dotnet run --project MemorySmith.Benchmarks -- --smoke` (`CodeSearch Relevance Scorecard: 5/5 passed`, warm averages about `0.56-0.59 ms`).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Audit #6 validation pass completed against the live repo instead of the report text alone. Confirmed: `CodeSearchService` still has the lexical-tail indentation defect, JSON `EmbeddingJson` persistence, non-pooled SQLite connections without WAL/perf PRAGMAs, scalar `Dot`, no query-result cache TTL, and single-character token dropping. Corrected stale audit claim: hybrid ranking weights are no longer hardcoded-only; they are already configurable through `MemorySmithOptions`, `appsettings.json`, and `AdminSettingsService`, with validation coverage already in place. Follow-up backlog split into validated tasks `TSK-0211` (code-search SQLite/storage hot path hardening) and `TSK-0212` (chat tool-call parse/buffer fallback hardening). Companion notes were added in `Data/Pages/audits/vector-search-audit-6-validation-20260528.md`.
